question: What is the primary purpose of hemostasis in the human body?

options.A: To produce new red blood cells in the bone marrow
options.B: To pump blood efficiently through the heart
options.C: To transport oxygen and nutrients to body tissues
options.D: To stop bleeding from injured blood vessels

explanation: Hemostasis is the specific physiological response designed to halt bleeding and repair vascular injury. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why is a delicate balance of hemostasis important for a patient?

options.A: It maintains the proper blood pH balance during heavy exercise
options.B: It controls the exact amount of iron absorbed from the diet
options.C: It prevents both uncontrolled bleeding and unwanted blood clots
options.D: It ensures the heart rate stays within a normal resting range

explanation: The body must carefully balance clotting so that injuries seal properly without forming dangerous blockages inside healthy vessels. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h1)

question: What happens immediately when a blood vessel is injured?

options.A: Smooth muscle in the vessel wall undergoes a vascular spasm
options.B: White blood cells rush to destroy the vessel walls
options.C: Red blood cells multiply rapidly in the local area
options.D: Large amounts of fibrin are immediately produced

explanation: The very first response to blood vessel damage is the contraction of smooth muscle to instantly narrow the vessel and reduce blood loss. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h2)

question: What causes platelets to stick together and form a temporary plug at an injury site?

options.A: A sudden drop in the overall body temperature
options.B: Contact with exposed collagen and released chemical messengers
options.C: An increase in red blood cell production by the liver
options.D: The direct action of white blood cells on the vessel wall

explanation: When platelets touch exposed collagen under the damaged endothelium, they activate, change shape, and release chemicals that attract more platelets to build the plug. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h2)

question: What triggers the extrinsic pathway of the coagulation cascade?

options.A: The rapid destruction of red blood cells in the spleen
options.B: Direct contact of blood with exposed collagen inside a vessel
options.C: Tissue factor released from damaged outside tissues
options.D: An increase in white blood cell counts during an infection

explanation: The extrinsic pathway is set in motion quickly when tissue factor leaks from injured cells outside the blood vessel. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h3)

question: How do the intrinsic and extrinsic pathways work together in the body?

options.A: They both activate a series of clotting factors that lead into the common pathway
options.B: They regulate the exact volume of blood pumped by the heart
options.C: They prevent platelets from sticking to healthy blood vessels
options.D: They work in opposite directions to dissolve unwanted blood clots

explanation: Both pathways act as separate starting points that eventually feed into the same shared sequence to produce a solid clot. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h3)

question: What is the main role of thrombin in the common pathway?

options.A: It prevents blood from clotting inside healthy vessels
options.B: It destroys excess platelets before they can form a plug
options.C: It causes smooth muscle in the vessel wall to relax
options.D: It converts soluble fibrinogen into insoluble fibrin strands

explanation: Thrombin acts as the key enzyme that turns liquid fibrinogen into solid fibrin threads to build the actual clot structure. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why is the formation of a dense fibrin mesh essential for wound healing?

options.A: It dilutes the concentration of red blood cells near the injury
options.B: It speeds up the removal of waste products from damaged tissues
options.C: It lowers the local blood pressure to stop bleeding instantly
options.D: It reinforces the weak platelet plug into a strong, stable clot

explanation: The fibrin mesh acts like concrete scaffolding, locking the platelets and blood cells together into a sturdy patch that stops bleeding securely. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h4)

question: What is the primary function of plasmin during the healing process?

options.A: It breaks down and dissolves the fibrin clot
options.B: It stimulates the rapid production of new platelets
options.C: It causes the initial vascular spasm in injured vessels
options.D: It converts inactive prothrombin into active thrombin

explanation: Plasmin is the active enzyme responsible for digesting fibrin strands so the body can clear away old, unneeded clots. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h5)

question: What happens during the process of clot retraction?

options.A: White blood cells destroy excess fibrinogen in the plasma
options.B: Platelets contract to pull the edges of the broken vessel together
options.C: The blood pressure drops to prevent further vessel damage
options.D: Red blood cells multiply to replace the lost fluid volume

explanation: Clot retraction tightens the meshwork and draws the wound edges closer, which makes tissue repair much easier. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h5)

question: What is the primary role of natural anticoagulants like antithrombin III?

options.A: To prevent unwanted clotting in healthy, uninjured blood vessels
options.B: To stimulate platelets to stick together during a vascular injury
options.C: To dissolve large clots that have already formed in the legs
options.D: To speed up the conversion of fibrinogen into solid fibrin

explanation: Natural anticoagulants keep the clotting system in check so that blood does not form dangerous clots where there is no injury. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h6)

question: How do healthy endothelial cells help prevent abnormal blood clotting?

options.A: By triggering the intrinsic pathway during normal circulation
options.B: By releasing substances that actively inhibit platelet sticking
options.C: By producing large amounts of active thrombin into the blood
options.D: By slowing down the heart rate to reduce blood turbulence

explanation: Intact endothelium produces chemicals like prostacyclin and nitric oxide that discourage platelets from clumping together on normal vessel walls. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h6)

question: Which laboratory test is most commonly used to monitor a patient taking warfarin?
explanation: Prothrombin Time and its standardized INR ratio are the standard tests used to track the effectiveness of warfarin therapy. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h7)

question: Why does a nurse monitor the activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) for a patient receiving heparin?

options.A: To measure the exact number of active platelets in the bloodstream
options.B: To check if the patient has developed an iron deficiency anemia
options.C: To ensure the intrinsic and common pathways are appropriately suppressed
options.D: To evaluate how well the liver is producing new red blood cells

explanation: Heparin affects the intrinsic pathway, so checking the aPTT lets the nurse know if the drug dose is safe and effective. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h7)

question: Which condition is characterized by inherited deficiencies in specific clotting factors?
explanation: Hemophilia is a well-known genetic disorder where the body lacks certain clotting factors, leading to prolonged bleeding episodes. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h8)

question: A patient with a bleeding disorder shows new petechiae and bruising on their arms. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: Administer a dose of oral aspirin to thin the blood safely
options.B: Apply a warm compress firmly to dissolve the bruises immediately
options.C: Report these physical findings and monitor closely for further bleeding
options.D: Encourage the patient to walk around the ward to improve circulation

explanation: New bruising or petechiae indicate a bleeding tendency, requiring prompt reporting and vigilant monitoring for more serious hemorrhage. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h8)
